capabilities.description: Constructs a policy-bound authenticated Terminal over one explicitly supplied capability.

attenuation.guidance: Prefer granting the already-constructed Terminal instead of the Authority constructor.

securityNotes: This is a policy-construction authority, not an application session.
Grant only to trusted system children with a documented need to construct Terminals.

capabilities.description: Spawns instances of one already-selected WASM image and reports that image CID.

attenuation.guidance: An Executor is already attenuated relative to Runtime because it cannot select another image.

securityNotes: Prefer Executor over Runtime whenever the child needs to spawn only one selected image.
The child must still supply each descendant's explicit grant map.

capabilities.description: Exposes node identity, addresses, peers, and the network listener/dialer capability bundle.

attenuation.guidance: Attenuate to the exact methods required, or grant a narrower capability returned by host.network().

securityNotes: network returns listener and dialer capabilities, so an unattenuated Host is broad node authority.
Catalog membership does not mean the current node or child possesses Host.

capabilities.description: Makes host-proxied HTTP GET and POST requests within the configured domain allowlist.

attenuation.mechanism: host domain allowlist plus optional hook-level method allowlist
attenuation.guidance: Use --http-dial for domain attenuation and optionally restrict the reference to get or post.

securityNotes: The reference is absent when no outbound host allowlist is configured.
Do not pass bearer tokens through args or env when a scoped capability protocol can carry the operation.

capabilities.description: Registers an image-bound Executor as an HTTP/WAGI handler with a fixed child grant template.

attenuation.guidance: The interface has one method; scope service prefixes through trusted configuration.

securityNotes: Obtained through host.network(); possession permits route registration.
Listener templates replay only the explicitly supplied child grants.

capabilities.description: Issues domain-scoped signers backed by the node identity and verifies Ed25519 signatures.

attenuation.mechanism: domain-scoped Signer plus optional hook-level method allowlist
attenuation.guidance: Prefer granting a Signer for one already-selected domain instead of Identity.

securityNotes: The private key remains host-side, but signing authority is still identity authority.
Ordinary children should receive a narrower Signer where possible.

capabilities.description: Delivers an ordinary child's immutable named initial capability references.

attenuation.guidance: This is supplied by the process bootstrap and is not an author-selected application grant.

securityNotes: get returns only the already-recorded references and cannot look up names.
It exposes no graft, refresh, append, discovery, or parent-channel operation.

capabilities.description: Streams IPFS-family paths through the node backend for non-WASI clients.

attenuation.guidance: WASI children should normally use their fixed content filesystem substrate instead.

securityNotes: This RPC capability is distinct from image-rooted and known-CID WASI reads.
Granting it exposes backend reads beyond the child's ordinary filesystem root.

capabilities.description: Returns the trusted root's configured host capability graft.

attenuation.guidance: Do not grant Membrane to ordinary children; delegate selected returned references instead.

securityNotes: Only trusted pid0 and separately authorized remote principals graft host authority.
Ordinary children receive InitialGrants, not Membrane.

capabilities.description: Provides DHT routing, IPNS resolution/publication, and immutable root-transform operations.

attenuation.guidance: Grant only the required methods, for example hash without provide, resolve, mutation, or publish.

securityNotes: provide, resolve, and publish have network or naming effects.
mkdir, writeFile, and remove construct new immutable roots and should be reviewed as content mutation.

capabilities.description: Loads arbitrary WASM bytes into image-bound Executors and can shut down its spawned tasks.

attenuation.mechanism: prefer image-bound Executor; optional hook-level method allowlist
attenuation.guidance: Load the intended image in the parent and grant its Executor unless the child truly needs arbitrary image selection.

securityNotes: Runtime is load-any-code authority and should require an explicit justification.
Executor is the canonical narrower alternative.

capabilities.description: Signs epoch-bound nonces within one domain selected when the Signer was created.

attenuation.mechanism: Identity.signer domain scope plus optional hook-level method allowlist
attenuation.guidance: Prefer this already-domain-scoped reference over Identity.

securityNotes: The reference carries signing authority even though key bytes never leave the host.

capabilities.description: Opens a named libp2p byte stream to an explicit peer.

attenuation.guidance: The interface has one method; use a wrapper when peer or protocol restrictions are required.

securityNotes: Obtained through host.network(); protocol names are locators, not authorization keys.

capabilities.description: Registers an image-bound Executor for a libp2p byte-stream protocol with a fixed child grant template.

attenuation.guidance: The interface has one method; scope protocols through trusted configuration.

securityNotes: Obtained through host.network(); possession permits protocol registration.

capabilities.description: Authenticates an epoch-bound signer and conditionally returns one configured session capability.

attenuation.mechanism: recipient policy plus hook-level method allowlist on the issued session
attenuation.guidance: Grant or publish the Terminal when the recipient must authenticate before receiving the session.

securityNotes: Possessing Terminal is not itself a successful login; the configured signing proof is still required.
The session it issues carries the application authority.

capabilities.description: Dials a named peer vat and returns its remote bootstrap capability.

attenuation.guidance: Wrap with a peer/protocol-specific application capability when a fixed destination is intended.

securityNotes: The service protocol is a locator, not an authorization key.
The returned remote capability is authority obtained through this dialing authority.

capabilities.description: Publishes an explicit capability on a raw or authenticated libp2p vat protocol.

attenuation.mechanism: authenticated policy or explicit raw publication plus hook-level membrane
attenuation.guidance: Prefer authenticated publication; raw publication is an explicit escape hatch.

securityNotes: serveRaw exposes the supplied capability to any peer that reaches the protocol.
Publishing a capability does not derive authority from the protocol name.
